updates.name: Jeffrey L. Collett Jr.
updates.bio: University Distinguished Professor of Atmospheric Science at Colorado State University, on the faculty since 1994 and department head from 2011 to 2022. His field-based research covers cloud and fog chemistry, nitrogen deposition, aerosol chemistry and haze, and air pollution from oil and gas development, agriculture and wildland fires, along with instrument development.
updates.research_interests: cloud and fog chemistry; nitrogen deposition; aerosol chemistry; air quality effects of unconventional oil and gas development; wild and prescribed fire emissions; precipitation and dew chemistry; ammonia exchange between atmosphere and surface; aerosol effects on visibility; instrument development
updates.current_affiliation: Department of Atmospheric Science, Colorado State University
updates.evidence: Jeffrey L. Collett, Jr. – University Distinguished Professor
updates.notes: The homepage on file (atmos.colostate.edu/people/jeffrey-collett/) now redirects to a 2025 award news item, so it is replaced by the department faculty profile (200). Lab site https://collett.atmos.colostate.edu/ (200) lists 'Air quality in U.S. National Parks' among research themes. ORCID on file re-checked: pub.orcid.org name Jeffrey Collett, employment Colorado State University, Professor, Atmospheric Science, 1994-present. The bio pronoun follows the profile page, which uses 'His interests'. Neither page links Google Scholar.

updates.name: Christopher Bowser
updates.bio: Leads education work for the NYSDEC Hudson River Estuary Program and the Hudson River Reserve, running community-science efforts such as the Eel Project and student projects under the Day in the Life program for the Hudson and Harbor. Earlier roles: Peace Corps reforestation volunteer in West Africa, Sloop Clearwater education director, and environmental science instructor at Marist and Bard.
updates.current_affiliation: NYSDEC Hudson River Estuary Program / Hudson River National Estuarine Research Reserve (New York State Water Resources Institute, Cornell University)
updates.evidence: Chris Bowser coordinates the education team at the NYSDEC Hudson River Estuary Program and Hudson River National Estuarine Research Reserve.
updates.notes: Profile is on the Cornell WRI people list (wri-people page lists 'Chris Bowser Education and Citizen Science Lead Hudson River Estuary Program'). updates.name: Lindsay R. Boring
updates.bio: First director of the Jones Center at Ichauway in southwest Georgia, chosen from a junior faculty post in forestry and natural resources (Warnell School) at the University of Georgia. Dr. Boring built the center's programs, staff and infrastructure, described its goal of research partnered with land managers so management is science based, and was succeeded by Kier Klepzig in 2017.
updates.current_title: Former Director (first Director), Jones Center at Ichauway
updates.evidence: identifying the Center’s first Director, Dr. Lindsay Boring, who was a young faculty member at the University of Georgia’s Warnell School
updates.notes: Source is the Center's report 'The History and Legacy of The Jones Center at Ichauway' (Bogue 2019, doi.org/10.58497/64952), linked from https://www.jonesctr.org/history-jones-center-at-ichauway-pub/ (200). It says 'Dr. Kier Klepzig succeeded Dr. Boring as Director of The Jones Center in 2017', which conflicts with the 1991-2014 tenure in the lake's title; the lake row should be checked. The report does not state emeritus or retired status, so status is left null. Boring is not on the current jonesctr.org staff list. The bio uses no pronoun. Verifier: bio reworded so it no longer says Dr. Boring 'championed' science-based management; the report only quotes a chapter describing that goal.
